prompt: Implement a concurrency-safe conditional notes HTTP API behind notes.NewHandler() http.Handler, using only net/http and the standard library. Each handler has isolated in-memory state. Match r.URL.Path exactly as /notes/{key}, where key matches [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}; all other paths return 404. Support GET, PUT, DELETE only; other methods return 405 with Allow: GET, PUT, DELETE. All nonempty response bodies are JSON with Content-Type application/json; every error is an object with a nonempty string error field (wording unspecified). GET existing returns 200 and exactly key,text,version fields, with version a positive integer and ETag the quoted decimal version, e.g. "1". GET missing returns 404. If GET's If-None-Match equals the current ETag exactly, return 304 with ETag and empty body; other values do not match. PUT must specify either If-None-Match: * for create-if-absent or If-Match: "N" for update-if-current. N must be positive uint64 canonical decimal (no leading zeros, signs, weak tags or lists). DELETE requires If-Match in that format; If-None-Match is invalid. Missing both precondition headers returns 428; malformed or conflicting headers return 400. Check precondition syntax before reading the body. With syntactically valid preconditions, validate PUT's body before checking current state: exactly one JSON object with exactly one supported field text, required and a non-null string; empty text is valid; unknown fields/additional JSON values/malformed JSON are 400. Text is limited to 4096 decoded UTF-8 bytes (overlong text is 400); encoded request body is limited to 16384 bytes including whitespace (larger is 413). Read failures are 400. Request Content-Type is ignored. Existence/version mismatch returns 412, including DELETE/If-Match on a missing note, with no state change. Successful PUT create returns 201 and update 200, each with the GET representation and ETag. Each key's first successful PUT is version 1; every subsequent successful PUT increments its previous version, INCLUDING recreation after deletion; DELETE keeps that counter. Successful DELETE returns 204 empty body. 304/204 need no Content-Type. DELETE ignores its body. Failed requests never change state. Preconditions and mutations must be atomic: simultaneous updates with the same ETag have exactly one winner. Tests use httptest and go test -race; no actual listener is needed. Add regression tests.
